newsitem.title: USA: Norwest Corp Q1 credit loss provisions up.
newsitem.headline: Norwest Corp Q1 credit loss provisions up.

text.p: Norwest Corp said Monday its first quarter provision for credit losses rose to $109.0 million from $87.8 million in the 1996 first quarter.
Norwest said the increased credit losses was due to higher levels of chargeoffs in regions that have had acquisitions and higher consumer credit chargeoffs.

Among its first quarter consumer past-due delinquencies, Norwest said, was a rise in credit card payments 30 days past due, rising to 4.12 percent of the total from 3.86 percent in the year-ago first quarter.
The percentage of its mortgage servicing portfolio 30 days past due increased to 5.6 percent in the first quarter from 4.4 percent a year ago.
Norwest also said its total non-interest income in the first quarter rose to $690.6 million from $552.8 million a year ago.
Norwest said the rise in non-interest income reflected growth in virtually all categories, including trust, fees and service charges, insurance and mortgage banking revenues.
Net interest income for the quarter rose to $958.3 million from $890.8 million.
